decisions.reason: As a flagship product closely aligned with the firm's sustainability direction, it is likely to receive managerial attention and slack resources, so early uncertainty alone would not trigger withdrawal.
A foldable large container line with several models and its own webpage signals commitment and likely acceptable early market feedback, making continuation more likely than problemistic search.
Although only mentioned rather than heavily featured, this stackable crate line fits the core reusable-packaging business and a large firm would usually keep it on the market while learning.

This pallet line is strategically related to the established offering, but its lower visibility suggests weaker proof of success, so it faces somewhat higher review risk yet is still more likely to be retained.

Its own page and multiple models indicate a meaningful launch effort in a complementary niche, and a large firm with organizational slack would likely continue unless results were clearly below aspiration.
The product has dedicated market presentation and fits the firm's logistics-packaging capabilities, so management would likely keep it for another year absent strong evidence of underperformance.
